title: Investigating the role of PmrB mutation on Colistin antibiotics drug resistance in Klebsiella Pneumoniae.
authors: Shahab, Muhammad; Waqas, Muhammad; Fahira, Aamir; Zhang, Haoke; Zheng, Guojun; Huang, Zunnan
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和MD模拟分析PmrB突变对粘菌素耐药性的影响，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作，但对象为细菌蛋白与抗生素，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联度低。
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae, a member of the Enterobacteriaceae family, naturally resides in the digestive tracts of both healthy animals and humans. Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) poses a significant health risk for hospitalized patients worldwide, greatly reducing the effectiveness of commonly used antibiotics. This leaves healthcare providers with limited treatment options, often relying on colistin. PmrB is important for the survival of Klebsiella pneumonia and, a mutation in the PmrB protein is accountable for the development of colistin antibiotic resistance in Klebsiella pneumonia. This is especially important because colistin is a fundamental component in the treatment of pneumonia. Three mutated residues-T157P, G207D, and T246A-are responsible for colistin resistance. The structural alterations and underlying mechanisms in the PmrB protein that cause resistance owing to mutation remain unclear. As a result, this study is focused to the exploration of the putative mechanism of resistance resulting from these mutations, as well as the structure modification of normal and mutant PmrB proteins, using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations analysis. Our results demonstrated that the interaction paradigm for the mutants has been altered and thus showing a significant effect upon the hydrogen bonding network. Interestingly, the binding of Colistin with the three mutant demonstrate unstable behavior as compared with WT(+Colistin). The proposed drug-resistance mechanism will help to guide the development of PmrB drugs. These finding may give a new framework for developing novel drugs against the mutant version of PmrB.
abstract_zh: 肺炎克雷伯菌（Klebsiella pneumoniae）作为肠杆菌科（Enterobacteriaceae）的一员，自然栖息于健康动物和人类的消化道中。耐碳青霉烯类肺炎克雷伯菌（CRKP）对全球住院患者构成重大健康威胁，显著降低了常用抗生素的有效性。这使得医疗提供者面临有限的治疗选择，往往依赖粘菌素（colistin）。PmrB对肺炎克雷伯菌的生存至关重要，而PmrB蛋白中的突变是导致肺炎克雷伯菌对粘菌素抗生素产生耐药性的原因。这一点尤为重要，因为粘菌素是治疗肺炎的基础药物。三个突变残基——T157P、G207D和T246A——负责粘菌素耐药性。由突变引起的PmrB蛋白结构改变及其耐药机制尚不清楚。因此，本研究旨在利用分子对接和分子动力学模拟分析，探索这些突变导致的耐药性可能机制，以及正常和突变型PmrB蛋白的结构修饰。我们的结果表明，突变体的相互作用模式已发生改变，从而对氢键网络产生显著影响。有趣的是，与WT（+粘菌素）相比，粘菌素与三种突变体的结合表现出不稳定的行为。所提出的耐药机制将有助于指导PmrB药物的开发。这些发现可能为开发针对突变型PmrB的新型药物提供新框架。
